brief: BofA's weekly volatility compendium runs three arguments plus two monitors. First, with US midterms about two months away and Kalshi showing a close Senate race, S&P options price only a 0.82% post-election move against a 1.3% average historical midterm reaction, and easing equity leverage plus low correlation point to rotation rather than an index vol shock, so BofA says avoid overpaying for index protection and prefers an SPX Dec26 95%/80% down-and-out put at 0.55%, a sold VIX Oct 16 put against a Nov 22-30 call spread, and IWM Nov 280 puts where regional banks and small caps look underpriced versus 2024 election-week moves. Second, SX7E dividend futures trade close to analyst estimates after 60% two-year gains, so remaining upside sits in SX5E dividends at Dec28 and Dec29, aided by ASML capping, and BofA rotates SX7E into SX5E divs or into European bank equities. Third, Kospi realised and implied vols have roughly halved and the Bubble Risk Indicator has fallen to 0.52 from above 0.8 at 6.2x forward earnings, so BofA moves from long gamma to a 3-month 110%/130% call spread part-funded by an 80% put. GFSI fell to -0.21, its third weekly decline in four, led by equities.
